subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Is the adjacent current-main `2>/dev/null` normalization coverage enough to close #87980, or should maintainers require an exact `2>&1` regression proof first?
rationale: Current source strongly supports the intended command-string contract, but the issue's primary `2>&1` examples were not directly reproduced or covered by the observed test.

options.title: Require exact regression proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a targeted `2>&1` regression test or live proof shows current main preserves the reported redirect cases.

options.title: Close from adjacent main proof
options.body: Close as effectively fixed on main based on the single-command-string runtime path and adjacent `2>/dev/null` normalization test.

recommendation.title: Require exact regression proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open until a targeted `2>&1` regression test or live proof shows current main preserves the reported redirect cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent normalization work and adjacent regression coverage make this the best available routing signal for the proof decision.
